title: Canonical representative identifications for convolution localization
statement: Use the finite filtered homotopy category [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy], its good subcategory [lem-kun-finite-filtered-kflat-replacement], and convolution [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison]. The finite representative is the same filtered complex with the proof of finite filtration; its good representative is its homotopy class with its goodness proof. Representative maps are the corresponding quotient maps. The convolution representative carries the supplied goodness proof. Localized representatives are their images under the fixed replacement equivalence. The lift identification is the composite of its inclusion square, the single-variable localization witness, the representative object equality and the ordinary quotient-to-derived comparison. The star identification is the composite of the transport comparison, inverse equivalence units, the two-variable localization witness and the representative object equality. The graded comparison is exactly the residue-class comparison selected by [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison], whose equation determines it uniquely. These are the existing ten definitions, moved unchanged in meaning into a common interface module.
